A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DICEPTION. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching renamed tasks and relocated results.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative evaluations of depth, normals, segmentation and human keypoints, together with architectural experiments and qualitative few-shot adaptation results.

after.justification: v3 retains original model evaluations and adds experiments on input conditioning, alternative architectures, guidance, inference steps and few-shot adaptation.

M1.justification: The RGB representation, point embeddings, flow-matching objective, LoRA adaptation and post-processing remain. v3 adds guided inference combining task-conditioned and empty-prompt predictions, with CFG=2 as the default, and presents a PixArt-alpha backbone variant. These extend the existing framework; expanded descriptions of token concatenation and RoPE alone do not establish changes to the original architecture.

E1.justification: The principal training datasets and benchmark suite in Table S1 are retained. v3 adds BAID/generated-image examples for detail preservation and exploratory referring-segmentation and point-conditioned depth-composition examples (Figures S7, S12 and S13). Renaming semantic segmentation to text-based instance segmentation, and point-prompted segmentation to interactive segmentation, does not itself add coverage.

E2.justification: v3 substantially expands targeted comparisons: ControlNet is evaluated for pose prediction, directly adapted SD3 for few-shot highlighting, and IC-Light for detail preservation (Figures S4, S6 and S7). The original quantitative benchmark comparator sets are retained. Removing the entirely blank Painter and One Diffusion rows from the normal-estimation table does not remove evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v3 adds controlled token/channel-concatenation experiments, a 600M-parameter PixArt configuration, CFG sweeps from 1 to 5, inference-step sweeps for DICEPTION and comparison models, and matched SD3 few-shot comparisons. Main depth/normal results now correspond to CFG=2; v1 values are reproduced as CFG=1 in Tables S6–S7. The retained benchmark metrics and main training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New Appendix B substantially expands analysis of input injection, backbone choice, ControlNet conditioning, guidance sensitivity, reduced-step inference, adaptation speed and detail preservation. Appendix E adds exploratory task-composition cases. The original U-Net failures, one-step-training failures, point-count comparison and post-processing error examples remain, sometimes relocated; those are not new analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new sweeps continue reporting point estimates. Surface-normal mean and median values are prediction-error metrics, not estimates of run-to-run uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 contain revised model results under the newly reported guidance setting: depth AbsRel changes from 0.072 to 0.061 on NYUv2 and from 0.243 to 0.289 on DIODE. These are not same-setting gains; the original rows survive as CFG=1 results. Unified-IO's DIODE delta1 changes from 0.906 to 0.708. Tables S2–S12 add extensive backbone, guidance and inference-step results, including segmentation mIoU of 47.10 at 28 steps versus 42.53 at one step. Main pose, entity and instance-segmentation scores are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds an explicit mathematical definition of the guided prediction as a combination of conditional and unconditional outputs (Equation S1). The original flow-matching objective and point-embedding definitions remain equivalent. No new theorem or proof is provided; the explanations involving denoising trajectories are qualitative.

C1.justification: v3 adds a qualified priority claim for a fully shared multitask model achieving specialist-comparable performance with much less data. Its central contributions now emphasize preserving pretrained priors, guidance benefits, pixel-aligned training and matting-level detail preservation. The conclusion also removes v1's qualification that performance may be acceptably below specialist models. The original data-efficiency and few-shot-adaptation claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds mechanisms linking guidance sensitivity to pixel precision, few-step inference to flow-matching trajectories, and detail preservation to pixel-aligned training. It distinguishes unsuccessful one-step training from successful reduced-step inference after multistep training. Small-object entity-segmentation weaknesses are reattributed from limited-data overfitting in v1 to post-processing in v3. New task-composition discussion explicitly acknowledges a very low success rate.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents aligned RoPE positions for input/noisy tokens, empty negative prompts, the guidance default, ControlNet placement in the first half of SD3 blocks, and the 600M PixArt backbone. It also specifies random selection of the five evaluation points and replaces project/demo pointers with a code-and-model repository link. Existing optimizer, hardware, training-duration and LoRA details are largely retained.

R1.justification: The Related Work sections and central positioning around pretrained diffusion priors are largely retained. v3 adds references to PixArt-alpha, classifier-free guidance, BAID/BacklitNet, RoFormer and IC-Light, strengthens its qualified novelty claim, and adds targeted positioning concerning few-step inference and detail preservation.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion are substantially rewritten. A method overview replaces the preliminary subsection, experimental analysis is reorganized, U-Net discussion moves into the expanded appendix, and one-step failures move into the main text. Post-processing discussion gains separate subsections, limitations become a broader discussion section, and task terminology is revised throughout.

P2.justification: v3 changes the document to a predominantly single-column layout, redraws the pipeline as a multi-panel diagram, and replaces the opening visualization arrangement. The original point-count bar chart becomes Table 5, while existing failure figures are relocated. Numerous new ablation tables, plots and comparison panels are added; most earlier appendix visualization grids are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 substantially strengthens evidence for design choices that v1 supported only sparsely. Controlled conditioning comparisons, alternative-backbone tests, guidance sweeps and inference-step experiments clarify how the framework works and distinguish one-step-training failure from useful few-step inference. Added SD3 comparisons also strengthen the adaptation argument. Some expanded claims remain insufficiently qualified, especially specialist parity and attributing low scores entirely to post-processing, and uncertainty reporting remains absent. Nevertheless, the new experimental evidence substantially improves support for the paper's central design and efficiency arguments.
